speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and arm weakness first started, and have they gotten worse throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing, especially later in the day? Has your breathing ever felt short or labored?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing, particularly later in the day? Has your breathing ever felt short or labored?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids, especially later in the day after using your eyes? Given your symptoms, I would like to order some specific tests to confirm my suspicion. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Neurological Examination reveals ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze. Motor strength is diminished in the upper extremities. Blood tests show elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies. Electromyography with repetitive stimulation shows decreased muscle response. Chest CT is normal with no thymoma detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of ptosis, fluctuating weakness, and positive antibody tests confirms a diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
